routes.named_ctr_finished_article: Pulp and pulp products of any fruit
routes.standard_definition: FSSR 2.3.33 defines Fruit Cheese as an as-sold set cooked product from fruit pulp/puree and salt/sweeteners; total soluble solids at least 65%, prepared fruit at least 45% except strawberry/raspberry at least 25%.
routes.positive_named_source_basis: CTR IX §2.1.1 lists pulp and pulp products of any fruit as a separate metal article. A finished Fruit Cheese may require official classification as a cooked pulp product, not merely proof that fruit pulp was an ingredient.

article_values.article: Pulp and pulp products of any fruit
article_values.analytical_basis: as-sold marketed cooked fruit pulp product; only if legally classified under this article

article_values.article: Pulp and pulp products of any fruit
article_values.analytical_basis: as-sold marketed cooked fruit pulp product; only if legally classified under this article

article_values.article: Pulp and pulp products of any fruit
article_values.analytical_basis: as-sold marketed cooked fruit pulp product; only if legally classified under this article

positive_product_evidence: Batch label/specification affirming as-sold fruit cheese standardized in FSSR 2.3.33, not jam/jelly/marmalade or fruit confectionery under a different legal article.
Recipe includes fruit species and actual starting pulp/puree %, salt/sweeteners, total soluble solids and finished set form.
Manufacturer process record for cooking, concentration/evaporation, packaging and applicable final sample basis.
Qualified formal ruling or documented supported CTR IX interpretation confirming that specific marketed cooked fruit cheese qualifies as 'Pulp and pulp products of any fruit'.
If article qualification fails, no fruit-pulp specific metal numeric limit is assigned; independently assess applicable general and finished-specific provisions.
forbidden_transfers: Do not inherit the CTR 'Jam, Jellies and Marmalade' tin article by resemblance to jam.
Do not infer raw fruit metal or pesticide residue figures on the cooked finished product without a supported process factor.
Do not classify a finished fruit sweet as an unprocessed fruit-pulp article from an ingredient list alone.
Do not claim a product compliance PASS or automatically compare a batch against the source values.
Do not treat the FSSR 65% soluble solids and required fruit % as contaminant article proof.
Do not infer actual shelf pack or processing evidence from the FoSCoS category.

routes.named_ctr_finished_article: Food colouring other than synthetic colouring
routes.standard_definition: FSSR 2.3.65 defines colouring foods as edible fruits/vegetables/spices/herbs processed by aqueous extraction without selective pigment extraction, retaining essential food characteristics, used as ingredients primarily for colouring; liquid and powder forms have distinct solids/marker standards.
routes.positive_named_source_basis: CTR IX §2.1.1 arsenic separately names 'Food colouring other than synthetic colouring' on dry colouring matter basis. A product meeting 2.3.65 remains an ingredient, and must be explicitly shown legally within the CTR non-synthetic colouring article before any arsenic value applies.

article_values.article: Food colouring other than synthetic colouring
article_values.analytical_basis: dry colouring matter basis, NOT dry final powder / whole ingredient basis; confirm official legal classification

positive_product_evidence: Identity/specification showing the product is a 2.3.65 colouring food, not a selectively extracted pigment, lake, or isolated synthetic colouring additive.
Recipe/plant origin and proof of aqueous extraction without selective pigment extraction; actual liquid or powder finished form.
Evidence for suitable analytical denominator 'dry colouring matter' separately from total dry solids and the marker pigment %.
Qualified formal interpretation or source-backed legal mapping of this exact food ingredient to CTR 'Food colouring other than synthetic colouring'.
Review lead 'Food colours other than caramel' and copper 'Colouring matter' separately rather than borrowing those numerics from this arsenic-only source route.
forbidden_transfers: Do not infer that the FSSR marker pigment minimum is the regulatory dry colouring matter result.
Do not copy lead source for 'Food colours other than caramel' to all 2.3.65 colouring foods automatically.
Do not borrow copper's 'Colouring matter' entry without an independent marketed ingredient classification.
Do not apply isolated dye, synthetic pigment or titanium dioxide metal impurity limits to a plant-derived colouring ingredient.
Do not imply a food colouring contaminant standard authorises particular additive use.
Do not automatically assign arsenic 5 mg/kg or declare any actual product or batch compliant.
